My 12-year-old son stepped onto the school stage to sing for the father he had lost three years earlier.

Caleb had changed after David died.

He stopped inviting friends over, often ate alone in his room, and whenever I asked what was wrong, he gave me the same answer:

“I’m fine.”

That was why I had been nervous about the school’s Father’s Day event.

I even considered keeping him home.

But Caleb insisted on going.

Then his name was called.

He walked onto the stage alone, carrying the old acoustic guitar David had taught him to play.

I had no idea he had prepared anything.

Caleb searched the audience until he found me.

Then he looked upward.

“This one is for my dad.”

The first notes nearly broke me.

It was the same song David used to hum in our kitchen on Saturday mornings.

By the second verse, several parents were wiping their eyes.

Even the teachers along the wall had gone completely still.

Then, without warning, the doors at the back of the gym opened.

Two uniformed police officers walked inside.

One of them looked toward Caleb.

Then he slowly removed his hat.

And when my son saw what the officer was holding in his other hand, he suddenly stopped singing.
